data.body:
CLOSING EVIDENCE — all five criteria met. Merged as Gerrit 1307, commit on main verified.

WHY THIS TICKET MATTERED BEYOND ITSELF: it was the only open ticket declaring `blocks 061c`, and it is the
hard prerequisite for eb6es Bedrock-provenance acceptance criterion — an `LLM-Review` vote whose sidecar
shows provider == "bedrock" was UNSATISFIABLE while code-review verdicts carried no provenance at all.

THE WIRING, verified by me at each cited line rather than taken from the implementers report:
  code-review.yaml:234   provider_provenance: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.provider_provenance }}
    Sourced from Pass-2 `verify`, an AGENT step whose outputs are the runner result VERBATIM — so this
    carries the record the runner already assembled rather than a second, possibly divergent one.
  workflow_ops.py:540-542  provenance = ctx.inputs.get("provider_provenance"); set only when not None.
  finalize.py:228 _verify_step_provenance(rec) reads the record back off the recorders succeeded verify
    step; :270-272 stamps it beside setdefault("model", cfg.model), again only when present.
  gate_dispatch.py — docstring only, recording why the degraded/outage path deliberately omits the key.

TWO CONSTRAINTS FROM THE PLAN, both honoured and both load-bearing:
  NOT RECOMPUTED. capabilities.provenance_fors docstring forbids recomputation because a second
    resolution can silently diverge from the record that actually drove the run. The existing record is
    threaded through; nothing calls capabilities_for again.
  NOT VIA THE USAGE AGGREGATE. Confirmed sizing.usage_record builds each per-call record from the runner
    results _usage SUB-DICT only, while provenance is stamped at the result TOP level — so that route
    drops it, exactly as the plan warned.

RED PROVEN THREE WAYS, and this is the part that matters, because story 343b nearly shipped this same
feature with a hole: its GAP 5 post-mortem records that all 10 of its unit tests passed while the field
never reached a production payload, because "every test hands build_payload a verdict dict that ALREADY
contains provider_provenance — a textbook constructed-input pass: the oracle proved the persist step, not
the path." So the oracle here runs the REAL code-review.yaml through the real interpreter, real scripted
ops and a real PydanticAIRunner (model swapped for FunctionModel), feeding its terminal verdict to the real
sidecar build_payload. No hand-built verdict anywhere in that path. Deleting each half in turn:
  YAML wire deleted        -> 3 failed  ("the record the runner stamped on the Pass-2 verify step is not
                                         reaching the verdict"; assert None; KeyError)
  op assignment deleted    -> 2 failed  (same oracle + KeyError) — so the oracle fails on EITHER half
  finalize backstop deleted-> 1 failed  (KeyError on the unwired-verdict recovery case)
  All restored: 7/7 green.
NOTABLY STRONGER THAN THE EXISTING PRECEDENT: the plan-review analogs oracle does NOT fail if its YAML
wire is removed. This one does. That is the 343b lesson applied rather than merely cited.

PER-AC:
  AC1 real assembly path carries it, and the real sidecar payload records it —
      test_a_real_gate_verdict_carries_provenance_into_the_sidecar_payload, asserting equality plus a JSON
      round-trip (a sidecar is serialized before signing).
  AC2 the YAML wires from an AGENT step — test_code_review_yaml_wires_provenance_from_an_agent_step
      resolves the wired step id back into the document and asserts that step has a `prompt`, so sourcing
      from a scripted op would fail.
  AC3 the degraded verdict OMITS the key rather than deriving one —
      test_the_degraded_verdict_omits_provenance_rather_than_deriving_one, plus the None-wire and
      no-record cases. A cfg-derived record where nothing ran would reproduce the exact defect provenance
      exists to remove.
  AC4 setdefault("model") accompanied by a provenance assignment — finalize.py:270-272, the two lines
      immediately following it.
  AC5 800-LOC cap — finalize.py 325, workflow_ops.py 703, gate_dispatch.py 560. All verified by me.

GATES, by exit code from the worktree venv on a clean tree: make lint = 0 · make typecheck = 0 (421 files) ·
check_config_reads.py = 0 · gen_env_registry.py --check = 0 · full suite = EXIT 0, 9556 passed, 41 skipped.
Plus Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 before submit.

PLAN VS REALITY, recorded: the plan cited commit b872bc3c89 and line numbers had shifted (code_review_coach
at workflow_ops.py:501-533 not 500-532; _degraded_code_review_verdict at gate_dispatch.py:260-280 not
246-257), but every substantive claim held. One overstatement: the coach input schema was already
`additionalProperties: true`, so no schema change was strictly required — the property was added for
documentation parity with plan-review, not for validation.
